item.content:encoded:
STAFF from Fiji’s Ministry of Women, Children, and Social Protection delivered essential supplies and clothing to vulnerable residents at the Grace Home Shelter and the Golden Age Home, with support from Mark Apparel.

Led by Acting permanent secretary Selina Kuruleca, the initiative aimed to support former street dwellers in residential care and assist a staff member affected by a fire, reinforcing the ministry’s commitment to community welfare.

In a statement the Ministry of Women, Children, and Social Protection said the donated items would benefit street dwellers who had recently been integrated into residential homes and shelters over the past few weeks, helping them rebuild their lives with dignity and hope.

item.title: BACK IN HISTORY | Fiji’s past comes alive | Museum holds second exhibition
item.description: In 1991, the Fiji Museum celebrated the nation’s diverse history with its second temporary exhibition, Fiji’s Early Settlers, featuring artefacts from various communities that settled in Fiji According to a report in The Fiji Times on June 5 that year, the exhibition ran from June 1 to August 31.
item.content:encoded:
In 1991, the Fiji Museum celebrated the nation’s diverse history with its second temporary exhibition, Fiji’s Early Settlers, featuring artefacts from various communities that settled in Fiji

According to a report in The Fiji Times on June 5 that year, the exhibition ran from June 1 to August 31.

The chief manager of the National Bank of Fiji at the time, Visanti Makrava, opened the exhibition.

“Exhibitions such as this were not just about objects of the past but provided us with an understanding that would benefit our future directions,” he said.

He said the program of the events would “enable a deeper understanding of the rich cultural heritage that the early settlers had left as their contribution to Fiji’s present society.”

“As such, these exhibitions should be seen as a vehicle for providing this and future generations with a compassion and understanding for moving into the future.”

The program of events included storytelling, talks, film, dress, and dance.

The exhibition opened with “a fashion parade from the National Dance Theatre of Fiji, then wearing traditional dress and dances from the Indian, Chinese, Rotuman and Banaban communities in Fiji.”

Addressing about 100 people who attended the opening, Ratu Meli Bainimarama, chairman of the Fiji Museum Board of Trustees, said the aim of the Temporary Exhibition Program was threefold.

“The museum housed the most comprehensive collection of traditional Fijian artefacts in existence, as well as smaller Pacific and historical collections,” Ratu Meli said.

“Only a third of this collection was on display at any one time, and therefore the temporary exhibitions allowed the museum to display artefacts that would otherwise be kept in store.”

“The exhibitions were also intended to publicise and generate ongoing interest in the museum’s national collections and were aimed at promoting Fiji’s rich cultural heritage.”

The exhibition was the second in a series of three and was part of a Temporary Exhibitions Program opened the previous year.

Each exhibition ran for three months and was organised in association with the Fiji Arts Council then.

The first one, titled Fijian Pottery – Past and Present, opened the previous November and featured examples from the museum’s extensive collection of traditional Fijian pottery.

Also included in the program were “pieces by three contemporary Fijian potters, pottery firing and pottery making demonstrations, testing sessions of food cooked in the traditional kuro and talks on various topics of interest related to Fijian pottery”.

Ratu Meli said the exhibition “benefited the potters participating by giving them exposure to traditional pottery from the Museum’s collection”.

He said “potters from different areas were also able to share their skills”.

The third and final exhibition was titled Fiji’s Celebrations and ran from December 1, 1991, to February 29, 1992. The display aimed at looking at various aspects of celebrations cross-culturally.

The program of events included “tasting sessions of festival food, displays of cultural costumes, talks, film and dance.”

Sponsored by the Naitonal Bank of Fiji, it aimed to promote Fiji’s cultural heritage and to generate ongoing interest in the Museum’s national collection.

item.title: Ex-teacher jailed for raping teens
item.description: A FORMER teacher at a prominent school has been sentenced to 14 years and six months’ imprisonment for sexually violating three teenage boys, with the High Court finding he had gravely breached the trust placed in him as a teacher. Justice Usaia Ratuvili sentenced the 27-year-old yesterday after convicting him of five counts of rape and one count of sexual assault committed in 2024.
item.content:encoded:
A FORMER teacher at a prominent school has been sentenced to 14 years and six months’ imprisonment for sexually violating three teenage boys, with the High Court finding he had gravely breached the trust placed in him as a teacher.

Justice Usaia Ratuvili sentenced the 27-year-old yesterday after convicting him of five counts of rape and one count of sexual assault committed in 2024.

The court heard the former teacher violated the boys, aged 15 and 17, on separate occasions, where he forced them to perform sexual acts.

In sentencing, Justice Ratuvili said schools, particularly boarding schools, must be safe places where parents can confidently entrust their children to teachers and school administrators.

He said teachers stand in loco parentis, with a duty to care for the children in their charge by ensuring they are safe, fed and provided with an environment in which they can learn and rest.

Justice Ratuvili said the sentence reflected the seriousness of the offending, denounced the abuse of trust, and served as both a specific and general deterrent while allowing the offender an opportunity for rehabilitation.

The former teacher will be eligible for parole after serving 11 years and nine months of his sentence.

item.description: THE High Court in Suva has issued a bench warrant for a man charged with the attempted murder of police constable Senoveva Tikoduadua after he failed to appear in court yesterday. item.content:encoded:
THE High Court in Suva has issued a bench warrant for a man charged with the attempted murder of police constable Senoveva Tikoduadua after he failed to appear in court yesterday.

Constable Tikoduadua, the daughter of Defence and Veterans Affairs Minister Pio Tikoduadua, was struck by a vehicle while manning a police checkpoint in Laqere, Nasinu, in April. The vehicle was allegedly being pursued by police at the time.

Neither the accused, Mr Saimoni Rokotunidau, nor his lawyer, Jerry Dinati, appeared when the matter was called.

State lawyer Katarina Dugan told the court that the office had unsuccessfully attempted to contact Mr Dinati and had written to the Legal Practitioners Unit to obtain his business address.

Mr Rokotunidau is charged with one count each of attempted murder, unlawful possession of illicit drugs, going equipped for theft, serious assault, and refusing to have his fingerprints and photographs taken. He is yet to enter a plea. The case has been adjourned to August 4.

item.title: Rape accused acquitted
item.description: A RAIWAQA resident accused of raping his four-year-old granddaughter has been acquitted by the High Court in Suva after the prosecution failed to prove the charge beyond reasonable doubt. The State alleged that between December 1 and December 9, 2025, the man raped the child.
item.content:encoded:
A RAIWAQA resident accused of raping his four-year-old granddaughter has been acquitted by the High Court in Suva after the prosecution failed to prove the charge beyond reasonable doubt.

The State alleged that between December 1 and December 9, 2025, the man raped the child.

In a judgment delivered on July 28, Justice Daniel Goundar found the complainant’s evidence was inconsistent and unreliable on the central issue of whether any unlawful sexual act occurred.

The court noted the child initially described inappropriate touching, but later, when asked directly during re-examination, denied that her grandfather had touched her. The judge also considered evidence from a neighbour who testified that the child had said she had been told by her mother to make the allegation.

Justice Goundar found the medical evidence was inconclusive, with the examining doctor stating the redness observed could have been caused by irritation or infection and did not establish penetration.

The judge ruled that the prosecution had also failed to prove the lesser offence of sexual assault beyond reasonable doubt.

item.title: Police shifts drug wars tactics
item.description: THE battle against drug networks has become a constant game of adaptation, with syndicates changing tactics and police adjusting operations to counter the evolving threat. Assistant Commissioner of Police (ACP) Operations Kasiano Vusonilawe shared this yesterday saying police had recognised that criminals were constantly developing their own strategies, requiring police to change the way operation
item.content:encoded:
THE battle against drug networks has become a constant game of adaptation, with syndicates changing tactics and police adjusting operations to counter the evolving threat.

Assistant Commissioner of Police (ACP) Operations Kasiano Vusonilawe shared this yesterday saying police had recognised that criminals were constantly developing their own strategies, requiring police to change the way operations were carried out.

Responding to questions from this newspaper, ACP Vusonilawe said periods where the public may not see visible police activity did not mean operations had stopped.

“We’re (beginning to recognise) their plans to outwit our operation,” he said.

“So we cannot continue with one trend of operations. We have to keep on changing this around.”

He said joint operations between the Fiji Police Force and the Republic of Fiji Military Forces (RFMF) were carried out for specific cases, particularly those involving national interest.

ACP Vusonilawe said not every case required the deployment of the joint team, as routine matters were handled separately by the relevant agencies.

Speaking on the memorandum of understanding between the RFMF and other government agencies, including the police for Exercise Bougainville 2026, ACP Vusonilawe said the exercise would strengthen police preparedness and improve understanding of how both agencies could support each other.

ACP Vusonilawe said the Government had classified Fiji as being in a “war of drugs”, adding that law enforcement agencies had to remain prepared for emerging challenges.

item.title: $2m water profit | Water bottler posts six months results
item.description: PUBLICLY-LISTED producer and bottler of VaiWai Natural Artesian water and AquaSafe – Pleass Global Limited – has recorded a profit before tax of $2,590,069 for the six months ended June 30 this year. That represents a 17 per cent increase over the $2,208,333 recorded for the corresponding period in 2025.
item.content:encoded:
PUBLICLY-LISTED producer and bottler of VaiWai Natural Artesian water and AquaSafe – Pleass Global Limited – has recorded a profit before tax of $2,590,069 for the six months ended June 30 this year.

That represents a 17 per cent increase over the $2,208,333 recorded for the corresponding period in 2025.

Revenue also increased by 19 per cent to $16,087,964, which the company said reflected continued growth across the business and the strength of the company’s brands and operations.

Company chairman and joint chief executive officer Warwick Pleass said the company’s financial position continued to strengthen, with net assets increasing to $40.5 million as at June 30, 2026, compared with $33.1m recorded at the same time last year.

He said the company board had also approved an interim dividend of 10 cents a share, up from eight cents per share in the first half of 2025.

“These results reflect the continued dedication of our people, the strength of our brands, and the confidence our customers and stakeholders continue to place in Pleass Global,” Mr Pleass said in the company’s stock market announcement.

“Achieving strong revenue and profit growth, together with declaring an interim dividend of 10 cents per share, demonstrates the strength of our long-term strategy and our commitment to creating sustainable value for shareholders.

“We thank our employees, customers, suppliers and shareholders for their ongoing support.

“Based on our current performance and outlook, we remain confident in the company’s continued growth and future prospects.”

item.title: Five-star resort retains ISO status
item.description: FIVE-STAR resort Shangri-La Yanuca Island has retained its status as Fiji’s only resort certified for its Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Point (HACCP) system and the internationally recognised ISO 22000:2018 Food Safety Management System. The globally recognised food safety system establishes rigorous controls for identifying, managing and preventing potential food safety risks across culina
item.content:encoded:
FIVE-STAR resort Shangri-La Yanuca Island has retained its status as Fiji’s only resort certified for its Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Point (HACCP) system and the internationally recognised ISO 22000:2018 Food Safety Management System.

The globally recognised food safety system establishes rigorous controls for identifying, managing and preventing potential food safety risks across culinary operations.

Having successfully achieved recertification, the resort said reaffirmed its position as the country’s only resort certified to this internationally recognised food safety standard.

Resort general manager Francis Lee said following a stringent independent audit process, the recertification confirmed that comprehensive food safety practices remained embedded across the resort’s culinary process, from ingredient sourcing and receiving through preparation, service and ongoing monitoring.

“Achieving ISO 22000:2018 recertification is a significant milestone for Shangri-La Yanuca Island and reflects the dedication, teamwork and care demonstrated by our colleagues across the resort,” Mr Lee said in a statement from the resort.

“As Fiji’s only resort certified to ISO 22000:2018, we are proud to give our guests added confidence that every dining experience is supported by the highest standards of care and quality.”

Mr Lee said the certification extended beyond the resort’s seven restaurants and bars to include all colleague dining facilities and operational kitchens, covering a total of 15 food and beverage outlets.

He said their hygiene and sanitation team worked closely with colleagues across culinary, stewarding, purchasing and operations to ensure rigorous food safety practices were consistently upheld.

“As Fiji’s only resort certified to ISO 22000:2018, Shangri-La Yanuca Island, Fiji continues to set a benchmark for food safety excellence in Fiji’s hospitality industry, combining internationally recognized standards with authentic Fijian hospitality.”

In 2001, the Shangri-La Group introduced the Shangri-La Food Safety (SFS) Management System, developed around internationally recognised HACCP principles.

And since 2023, Shangri-La properties have further strengthened this commitment through ISO 22000:2018 Food Safety Management System certification, reinforcing a culture of continuous improvement and internationally recognised food safety practices.
